name: SVGX-DwT-10k Evaluation Set (DEval)
reason: Dataset not publicly available. Paper: 'Reason-SVG: Hybrid Reward RL for Aha-Moments in Vector Graphics Generation' (arXiv:2505.24499, published May 30, 2025). SVGX-DwT-10k dataset described in paper (10,000 SVG-DwT pairs with Drawing-with-Thought reasoning sequences) has not been released. HuggingFace profile xingxm has SVGX-Core-250k and SVGX-SFT-1M datasets but these lack the DwT reasoning component. SVGX-DwT-10k requires (T, C, O) triplets where T=text prompt, C=DwT reasoning (6-stage design process: concept sketching, canvas planning, shape decomposition, coordinate calculation, styling/color, final assembly), O=SVG code. Existing datasets only have (T, O) pairs without intermediate reasoning. Checked: no GitHub repo for Reason-SVG (author ximinng has other SVG projects but not this one); HuggingFace API confirms xingxm/SVGX-DwT-10k does not exist (401/404). Evaluation: DEval is 1,000-prompt held-out test set; metrics include FID, CLIPScore, HPSv2, SVG Validity, DwT Adherence, human evaluation. Multimodal benchmark (text-to-SVG with visual rendering evaluation) - can be onboarded with HEIM once dataset is released. Author likely preparing code/data release. Monitor: github.com/ximinng and huggingface.co/xingxm for updates.

ACL 2022 Workshop on When Creative AI Meets Conversational AI; 'Learning to Evaluate Humor in Memes Based on the Incongruity Theory'; authors: Kohtaro Tanaka, Hiroaki Yamane, Yusuke Mori, Yusuke Mukuta, Tatsuya Harada (University of Tokyo); dataset: 7,500 memes with real-valued humor annotations collected via crowdwork platform, refined to 1,411 memes after removing items with ambiguous ratings; task: binary classification to determine whether a given meme (image + caption) is humorous; based on incongruity theory which posits humor arises from incongruity between images and captions; models: based on ViLT and CLIP vision-language pretrained models; evaluation: classification accuracy using 10-fold cross-validation with 8 runs; key contribution: proposed refinement process to extract memes not influenced by interpersonal differences in humor perception, and method to explicitly extract and utilize incongruities between images and captions; findings: proposed approach outperformed other vision-language models in humor classification; no public dataset release found - Papers with Code lists 'No code available yet'; no GitHub repository or download links found; author website: https://kohtaro246.github.io/; NOTE: This is a multimodal vision-language task (image + text → humor classification); HELM supports multimodal evaluation through VHELM (Vision-Language HELM); rejection is solely due to dataset unavailability, not modality; future candidate for onboarding via VHELM if dataset becomes publicly available; ACL Anthology: aclanthology.org/2022.cai-1.9/

name: EXPOTION Multimodal Music Generation
reason: Music generation model training paper; trains specialized model for generating music from facial expressions, body motion, and text; not an LLM/VLM evaluation benchmark; evaluates generated audio quality, not language model capabilities

name: SciMON
notes: Scientific inspiration sentence generation; 194 human-verified gold subset from 2022 ACL papers; ROUGE-L/BERTScore against rel_sent references; repo renamed to EagleW/Scientific-Inspiration-Machines-Optimized-for-Novelty

name: TextLogo3K
notes: CVPR 2022 text logo layout generation benchmark. Multimodal: glyph images + character text → JSON bounding boxes [left,top,right,bottom] normalized to [0,1]. 300 test samples with 2-11 Chinese characters each (mean 4.8). 6 custom metrics (overlap, visual balance, alignment, MaxIoU, coordinate MSE, canvas utilization) all computable from JSON coordinates without rendering. Data on Google Drive (981MB zip, downloaded via gdown). Academic-use license.

name: ZeroSumEval
reason: Competitive evaluation framework, not a benchmark - requires head-to-head matches between models, incompatible with HELM's single-model evaluation pattern

name: CodeScientist Scientific Discovery Evaluation
reason: Research automation system, not evaluation benchmark; generates novel experiments dynamically through genetic mutation of papers/code; no standardized test set or ground truth; evaluation via human expert review for scientific soundness/novelty; ACL Findings 2025; cannot be used to evaluate arbitrary LLMs on fixed tasks

name: QUDsim
reason: Evaluation methodology/framework for measuring discourse similarity, not a benchmark; no specific evaluation task with ground truth labels

name: GODBench
reason: Multimodal (video-based); dataset not released

name: Measuring LLM Novelty as the Frontier of Original and High-Quality Output
reason: Dataset not yet publicly available - repository states 'Full code and data are coming soon'

name: Story Generation Evaluation on ROCStories and WritingPrompts
notes: Adapted from DeltaScore metric validation dataset; 20 ROCStories + 20 WritingPrompts prompts (40 total); originally contained pre-generated stories with human ratings, adapted to extract prompts+references for story generation benchmark; evaluated with BLEU/ROUGE; can optionally evaluate 5 dimensions (fluency, coherence, relatedness, logicality, interestingness)

name: MIXASSIST
notes: Reframed as text-only multi-turn dialogue: given conversation history + current user turn, predict assistant response. Filter has_content=True (156/250 test instances). audio_file paths skipped. input_history is a native Python list (no json.loads needed). Topics: drums(61), overall_mix(36), guitars(29), vocals(16), bass(10), keys(4). No associated paper. scenario: scenarios/mixassist/scenario.py

name: Arabic Story Generation Evaluation Framework
notes: Previously rejected as 'no formal evaluation' but paper has well-defined GPT-4-as-judge protocol with 5 dimensions (fluency, coherence, instruction following, consistency, variety) on 1-5 scale. Exact judge prompt in repo. Structured constraint-based prompts for children's story generation across 3 Arabic varieties. Supports dialect parameter (msa, egyptian, moroccan, all).

name: MARS
notes: Multimodal analogical reasoning over knowledge graphs (ICLR 2023). Images (76,424) require separate download from Google Drive or Baidu Pan. Text-only mode available using entity descriptions. 10,641 train, 1,020 dev, 1,362 test instances.

name: LLM-MA Balderdash
notes: Original data requires author contact; replaced with 50 curated obscure words (Wordnik Balderdash / Merriam-Webster) + 20 common words (Oxford 3000 control), all embedded in-code. Task: generate fake dictionary definition (model never sees real definition — faithful to game rule). Real definitions stored in-code for judge calibration only. LLM judge on 4 dims: convincingness, plausibility, dictionary_style, originality (1-5). Supports domain parameter: obscure | common | all.

name: BannerRequest400
notes: EMNLP 2025 multi-agent banner design benchmark (Sony). Multimodal: logo image + concrete request → JSON foreground design blueprint. 400 instances (100 advertisers × 4 audience/purpose pairs, 300x250 size). 6 LLM-as-judge metrics (TAA, LPS, AQS, CTAE, CPYQ, BIS) with strong human correlation (Pearson 0.854-0.955). Data downloaded from GitHub repo zip.

name: PodEval
reason: Evaluation framework, not a reusable benchmark. arXiv:2510.00485; 'PodEval: A Multimodal Evaluation Framework for Podcast Audio Generation'; provides a toolkit for evaluating podcast generation systems, not a fixed stimulus-response dataset; no standardized input prompts or ground truth labels; audio files not directly hosted (download links only, no programmatic access); evaluation metrics are audio-specific (DNSMOS, WER, speaker similarity, timbre) and not HELM-compatible; primary contribution is the evaluation pipeline architecture, not a benchmark for evaluating arbitrary LLMs.

name: SS-GEN
reason: Domain-specific educational content generation, not creativity; Social Stories are therapeutic materials for ASD with strict structural/pedagogical constraints (Carol Gray methodology); constraint-driven generation opposite of creative freedom; evaluates compliance with educational guidelines rather than creativity; dataset gated on HuggingFace; AAAI 2025; arXiv:2406.15695

name: Speak-to-Structure (S2-Bench)
notes: Same as TOMG-Bench (arXiv:2412.14642). NL instruction → SMILES string (text-in, text-out). 10 subtasks × 5K = 50K total; scenario defaults to 500/subtask = 5K. load_dataset() fails (mixed CSV/text formats); uses per-subtask hf_hub resolve URLs. Tier-1: SMILES syntax validity (no RDKit). Tier-2: constraint satisfaction via RDKit (atom counts, SMARTS, Tanimoto, property comparison). Fine-tuned Llama-3.1-8B outperforms GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet.

name: Creative Writing Tasks
notes: 9 subsets: dat (base), dat_thesaurus/etymology/opposites/random/young (5 strategies), synopsis, flash_fiction, haiku. 100 instances each (configurable). Same prompt repeated — measures creative output diversity. Custom metrics: GLoVe DAT score, BERT DSI, Lziv complexity. Nature Human Behaviour 2024.

name: Open-domain Dialogue Generation for Diversity
notes: 300 test examples; ArXiv 2412.03343; Multiple responses per context (default 5); Evaluation: semantic diversity (embedding similarity), n-gram diversity (Distinct-1/2), coherence (LLM judge 1-10 scale via Llama/GPT-4); PEFT framework for diverse response generation; annotator_notes.md included

name: Background and Hypothesis Pairs (BHP) dataset
notes: Biomedical hypothesis generation from research backgrounds; 387 examples (190 seen + 197 unseen splits); extracted by GPT-3.5/GPT-4 from literature; evaluated with BLEU/ROUGE; paper proposes 4 LLM-based metrics (novelty, coherence, scientific validity, feasibility); COLM 2024

name: ArenaHard v2.0
notes: Extracted creative_writing subset (250/750 prompts). Data: raw.githubusercontent.com/lmarena/arena-hard-auto/main/data/arena-hard-v2.0/question.jsonl filtered by category==creative_writing. Note: original benchmarks.json URL (facebookresearch/darling) was incorrect — corrected to lmarena/arena-hard-auto. LLM-as-judge on 4 dims (creativity, coherence, relevance, style_execution 1-10). Original benchmark uses pairwise ELO with GPT-4.1/Gemini-2.5.

name: CM3D (Chinese Multimodal Metaphor Mapping Dataset)
notes: Two subsets: detection (exact_match) and mapping (open_ended). Chinese-language. Images on Kaggle (743 MB, requires account). Annotations on gitfront.

name: LiveIdeaBench
reason: Dataset only has a train split; no test split available for evaluation.

name: IGA Intent-Guided Generation Evaluation
reason: System/model paper not evaluation benchmark; IGA is an intent-guided writing assistant (fine-tuned LM); releases training data (~1.2M examples across 7 intent types) and model checkpoint, not a standardized test set; evaluation was system-specific (automatic metrics, crowdsourced judgments, user study) to validate IGA vs baselines, not for benchmarking arbitrary LLMs; EMNLP 2021; arXiv:2104.07000

name: Design Problems Task (DPT)
notes: Adapted as generation task: 16 STEM design problems (5 accessibility + 3 transportation + 8 environment), prompts in-code. 830 human-rated responses in repo CSV for judge calibration. LLM judge on 5 dimensions: originality, cleverness, uncommonness, effectiveness, conciseness (1-5). Supports domain parameter.

name: MiQA (Metaphorical Inference Questions and Answers)
notes: 150 base examples generating 300 binary MC questions. Two question types: 'implies' (metaphor->conclusion) and 'implied_by' (conclusion->premise). Data in TSV from Google Research repo.

name: VBench-2.0
reason: Multimodal (video generation); requires HEIM framework. arXiv:2503.21755 (March 2025); part of VBench series (VBench CVPR 2024, VBench++ TPAMI 2025, VBench-2.0); comprehensive evaluation benchmark for video generative models covering text-to-video (T2V) and image-to-video (I2V) generation; VBench-2.0 extends VBench to evaluate intrinsic faithfulness for next-generation video models including commonsense reasoning, physics-based realism, human motion, creative composition; 5 broad categories and 18 fine-grained capability dimensions; original VBench has 16 dimensions: Quality (subject_consistency, background_consistency, temporal_flickering, motion_smoothness, aesthetic_quality, imaging_quality, dynamic_degree), Semantic (object_class, multiple_objects, human_action, color, spatial_relationship, scene, appearance_style, temporal_style, overall_consistency); evaluates video generation models like Gen-3, Kling, Pika, Sora, CogVideo across prompt suites; task: generate videos from text/image prompts and evaluate across multiple dimensions; uses automatic evaluation methods with alignment to human preferences; HuggingFace leaderboard with 40+ T2V models and 10+ long video models; requires vision models and video generation evaluation; outside HELM's text-only scope; would need HEIM framework for video evaluation; GitHub: Vchitect/VBench; PyPI package available

name: VideoCanvasBench
reason: Dataset not yet released - repository states "Code (Coming soon)" and "We will release this benchmark". Video generation task (arbitrary spatio-temporal video completion) not video understanding. Evaluates video diffusion models on visual quality metrics (FVD, PSNR, aesthetic quality). REVISIT when dataset released to assess text-based proxy tasks (e.g., describing completion strategies, predicting patch placement). Monitor: https://github.com/KwaiVGI/VideoCanvas
notes: Over 2,000 test cases (AnyP2V, AnyI2V, AnyV2V tasks). 100 high-quality videos from Pexels. Metrics: FVD, PSNR, temporal coherence, aesthetic quality. October 2025 paper.

name: ROBOTOOLBENCH
notes: Adapted URDF tool design + action planning task for LLM evaluation. 12 instances (one per RoboToolBench task), prompts generated in-code from paper task specs. Output = URDF XML + N×7 waypoint array. Tier-1 evaluation (HELM-computable): URDF validity, action array format. Tier-2 evaluation: PyBullet simulation reward (benchmark code coming soon at vlmgineer.github.io).

name: Fable Generation Evaluation Framework
notes: Previously rejected as 'training data, not benchmark' but the GitHub repo (klusai/tinyfabulist) contains a well-defined 100-prompt benchmark set with published baselines for 11 models. Evaluation uses o3-mini as judge on 4 dimensions (grammar, creativity, moral_clarity, adherence_to_prompt) on 1-10 scale plus age group classification. Prompts are combinatorial from 100+ characters/traits/settings/conflicts/resolutions/morals. Supports source parameter: 'benchmark' (100 prompts from paper) or 'full' (100K HF test split).

name: New Yorker Cartoon Caption Contest Humor 'Understanding' Benchmarks
notes: ACL 2023 Best Paper; 3 tasks (matching, ranking, explanation); text-only eval using cartoon descriptions; Matching: 5-way MC (9,792 train, 531 val, 528 test); Ranking: 2-way MC (9,576 train); Explanation: open-ended (2,340 train); Human 94% vs best model 62% on matching

name: Word2Minecraft
reason: Content generation system for creating Minecraft levels from stories using LLMs; no benchmark dataset or standardized evaluation framework; paper evaluates the Word2Minecraft system (GPT-4-Turbo vs GPT-4o-Mini) rather than providing a benchmark for testing arbitrary LLMs; outputs are game levels requiring specialized infrastructure; arXiv:2503.16536

name: CoMPAS3D
reason: Multimodal (requires 3D motion capture data, video, and audio); domain-specific dance/motion generation benchmark; HELM is text-only; not a text creativity task

name: LLM-SRBench
notes: ICML 2025 Oral; 239 scientific equation discovery problems across 5 subsets; gated HF dataset (nnheui/llm-srbench) requires HF_TOKEN; data in HDF5; evaluation requires executing predicted equations against test data (NMSE/R²); original benchmark uses iterative code generation, adapted for single-turn text equation output

name: Style-conditioned Quatrain Generation Evaluation
reason: Model implementation (ByGPT5) with training data release, not an evaluation benchmark. Repository contains: (1) token-free transformer model code, (2) QuaTrain training corpus (2.7M English + 5.9M German quatrains), (3) pretrained model checkpoints, (4) generation scripts. No standardized test set with ground truth quatrains for LLM evaluation. Paper (ACL 2023) compares ByGPT5 to baselines but doesn't define a reusable benchmark dataset. Performance benchmarking measures speed/memory, not poetry quality.
paper: ByGPT5: End-to-End Style-conditioned Poetry Generation with Token-free Language Models (ACL 2023)
notes: QuaTrain is a large-scale training dataset for poetry generation, not a benchmark. For poetry evaluation, consider alternative benchmarks with test sets.

name: ProteinBench
notes: Adapted Sequence Design subtask for LLM evaluation. 80 instances (4 lengths × 20 functional targets), prompts generated in-code. Evaluation requires bioinformatics pipeline (ESMFold + TM-align); see metric_notes.md. Validity (correct length + standard AA codes) can be computed without bioinformatics tools.

name: Calligrapher Typography Benchmark
notes: 100 test images; diffusion model benchmark for text style customization; metrics: FID, CLIP, DINO, OCR accuracy; self-reference and cross-reference tasks; data in Calligrapher_bench_testing.zip on HuggingFace

name: WikiArt (I Dream My Painting)
reason: Method paper, not a reusable benchmark. WACV 2025; introduces multi-mask inpainting method connecting MLLMs with diffusion models; task is text-guided multi-mask inpainting (image generation) requiring HEIM framework; uses WikiArt dataset (116,475 images) with automatic annotations from Kosmos-2 (global) and LLaVA (object-level), not human ground truth; evaluation metrics (FID, LPIPS, PSNR, CLIP-IQA) measure image generation quality; no standardized protocol for evaluating arbitrary models; primary contribution is method architecture (fine-tuned LLaVA for prompt generation + Stable Diffusion with rectified cross-attention for inpainting), not benchmark dataset; requires vision models and image generation evaluation capabilities outside HELM's text-only scope; would need HEIM for image generation evaluation; GitHub: cilabuniba/i-dream-my-painting

name: CreativePair
notes: ⚠️ Dataset not yet publicly released (authors: Alibaba Group / USTB); scenario is complete and ready to run once data is obtained; multimodal task (MultimediaObject with 2 images + text); 1,729 test pairs; labels: A or B (CTR winner, >60% gap, >1K impressions each); full 10-question Creative Evaluation Protocol embedded verbatim; prompt verbatim from paper Section 3.2

name: Oogiri-GO Standard Evaluation
notes: CVPR 2024; HF dataset viewer broken (encoding error on images.zip) but JSONL files load fine; 130K+ samples EN/CN/JP; MC humor discrimination from star-rated multi-response groups; images.zip 1.3GB; 1020 EN groups with 4+ star-rated responses

name: Credal Set Analysis for Creative Variability
reason: Methodology paper, not a reusable benchmark. arXiv 2509.23088; proposes credal set geometric framework for analyzing creative variability and uncertainty calibration; repository contains only analysis results (uncertainty_analysis.csv with 10K rows: 500 prompts × 20 model-strategy combinations) and summary tables; does not provide the actual 500 WritingPrompts used, the 10 human continuations per prompt, or any way to evaluate new models on same data; primary contribution is the analysis methodology (decomposing epistemic vs aleatoric uncertainty, calibration measurement) not a standardized benchmark; results show best model-human calibration of 0.434 (Gemma-2B); would need to reproduce their WritingPrompts selection process to use as benchmark

name: Scientist-Bench
reason: Research automation system, not evaluation benchmark; AI-Researcher is autonomous research system automating full pipeline (literature review, hypothesis generation, algorithm implementation, manuscript preparation); Scientist-Bench evaluates AI-Researcher system-specific capabilities, not arbitrary LLMs; open-ended research tasks without standardized creativity evaluation; similar to CodeScientist and The AI Scientist; NeurIPS 2025; arXiv:2505.18705

name: Crowd Vote
notes: Prompt templates verbatim from paper (arXiv:2509.09702, CC-BY-4.0); 3 task types: insights (≤10 words), ideas (≤50 words), wild_ideas (≤50 words); 100 curated brands × 3 types = 300 instances; specific 100 brands from original study not public — replaced with well-known brands across same 12 categories; LLM judge replaces pairwise crowd voting (678 ad professionals); judge assesses originality, brand_relevance, creative_potential, conciseness (1–5 each)

default.description: Open-ended scientific idea generation from single-keyword prompts across 22 scientific domains

name: LLM Discussion (AUT, Similarities, Instances, Scientific)
notes: 4 classic divergent thinking creativity tests (120 total items). (1) AUT: 30 objects, creative uses. (2) Similarities: 30 pairs, ways two things are alike. (3) Instances: 30 categories, name things in category. (4) Scientific: 30 scientific creativity questions across 5 types. All use LLM-as-judge on 4 dimensions: Fluency (count), Flexibility (count), Originality (1-5), Elaboration (1-5). Judge: GPT-4 or GPT-3.5. Subsets: aut, similarities, instances, scientific, all. Paper: COLM 2024 (arXiv:2405.06373).

name: Research Idea Execution Study
notes: Task reframed as LLM peer review (not execution): given a structured research idea, generate expert review on 5 dimensions (novelty, excitement, feasibility, expected effectiveness, overall); human expert execution replaced by LLM-as-judge; Tier-1 data from Google Drive zip (human ideas, file ID: 1Z2Nd7WNNks-eCoqUgPzx1_ovYqU8OiPx); Tier-2 fallback from GitHub idea_examples_method.json (10 guaranteed instances); 398 expert reviews in reviews_ideation/data_points_all_anonymized.json used for judge calibration

name: JUDGE Model Evaluation on OpenReview
reason: Meta-evaluation, not creativity. Paper is 'Spark: A System for Scientifically Creative Idea Generation' (arXiv:2504.20090). Judge is a reviewer model trained on 600K OpenReview reviews to predict accept/reject. Original dataset (spiralworks/openreview_wildcard_2025_v2) deleted; spiralworks has 0 public datasets. Author's archive has fragments: sumukshashidhar-archive/openreview-100k (98K reviews with idea_only_review_* fields from DeepSeek-V3 transforms, ICLR+NeurIPS 2017-2023), sumukshashidhar-archive/openreview-classification (2009 train/503 test, full paper text→accept/reject), sumukshashidhar-archive/openreview-decision-classification-benchmark (1284 train/321 test, abstract→accept/reject). Task is review prediction, not creative generation.

name: Human Evaluation of Generated Prose for Paintings
reason: Method paper, not a reusable benchmark. ICCV Workshop 2019, arXiv:1910.03634; 'Prose for a Painting'; proposes pipeline for generating Shakespearean prose descriptions of paintings using intermediate poem generation (image → poem via img2poem model) then language style transfer (poem → Shakespearean prose via text style transfer model); demonstrates approach on unspecified number of 'famous paintings'; evaluation mentions human ratings on Likert scale and BLEU score 'as a function of prose length' but provides no specifics (number of raters, scale range, rating criteria); **Key issues**: (a) No publicly available test dataset of paintings with ground truth Shakespearean prose, (b) Paper explicitly states 'there does not exist a large supervised dataset from paintings to Shakespearean prose', (c) Repository contains only demonstration notebook with single test image, no benchmark data, (d) No standardized evaluation protocol that other papers can follow, (e) Primary contribution is the method/pipeline architecture, not a dataset for evaluating other models; **Precedent**: Similar to PlotMachines (line 168 in LEARNINGS.md) rejected as 'Method paper, not a reusable benchmark'; requires downloading and training two separate models (img2poem + style transfer) from external repos with Dropbox models; if authors later release curated test set with human-written Shakespearean prose for paintings plus standardized evaluation, this could become a valid benchmark; GitHub: prerna135/prose-for-a-painting
notes: Method paper demonstrating image→poem→Shakespearean prose pipeline; no test dataset or standardized evaluation

name: Metaphoric Analogies from Literary Texts Dataset
notes: 203 examples; extracts 4-term metaphoric analogies from literary texts; some terms may be implicit (require inference); paper uses lemmatized head noun match, approximated with standard NLG metrics in HELM

name: Chinese Lyric Generation Evaluation
reason: Non-English (Chinese); research study, not benchmark; MojimLyrics dataset (39K songs) is training corpus; human evaluation primary (coherence, creativity); paper notes MAUVE metric has limitations for creative writing; no evaluation framework for new models

name: CreativEval
reason: Domain-specific (Verilog hardware) with impractical eval pipeline. IEEE LAD 2024. 120 HDLBits prompts (111 single-module + 9 multi-module). TTCT-based creativity framework (fluency, flexibility, originality, elaboration) is sound, but evaluation requires GNN4IP (circuit similarity via graph neural network) and Icarus Verilog (simulator for functionality testing), plus multi-generation per prompt (t=10). Does not fit HELM single-turn architecture. Repo is WIP.

name: Time-Bench
reason: Method paper for RL training framework; not a creativity benchmark. arXiv 2505.13508 (May 2025); Time-R1 is a 3-stage RL curriculum for temporal reasoning; Time-Bench dataset (200K+ examples) for training on timestamp inference, time-gap estimation, event ordering, masked time entity completion; Stage 3 'creative generation' is future news scenario prediction (temporal forecasting, not general creativity); evaluation tied to RL framework with custom reward functions (1200+ lines in time_reasoning.py); requires veRL infrastructure and PPO training; HuggingFace dataset (ulab-ai/Time-Bench) exists but designed for RL training, not standalone evaluation; primary contribution is training methodology, not a reusable benchmark for evaluating arbitrary models on creative tasks

name: Another Turn, Better Output?
reason: Dataset not publicly available
notes: Evaluation framework for iterative LLM prompting across ideation, code, and math domains. 12-turn conversations per task with vague/targeted feedback. Ideation domain evaluates originality and feasibility (creativity-relevant), but no public dataset found. No GitHub repo, HuggingFace dataset, or data availability statement. Only supplementary materials on OpenReview (openreview.net/forum?id=nPgh13kzhW). NeurIPS 2025 Workshop (Multi-Turn Interactions). If dataset becomes available, ideation domain could be onboarded.

name: MOH-X
notes: Dataset from gao-g/metaphor-in-context (EMNLP 2018), not the LAG paper; 647 verb-sentence pairs, binary metaphor/literal labels; Google Drive zip (file ID: 1-v_sUlupDrKq8ERlnh5RwdI7Pyk-6cxn) via gdown; no predefined split so all 647 used as TEST_SPLIT; prompt follows LCC Metaphor precedent

name: VGSG (Visually Grounded Story Generation)
notes: Uses VWP val split (849 examples, test has no labels). Multi-image: 5-10 scene images + character portraits per instance. ~7K images total.

default.description: Generate story from sequential movie images + character info

name: EmoArt
notes: Emotion classification from artistic images. Vision-language task where models classify the dominant emotion (12 categories: Alarmed, Annoyed, Aroused, Bored, Calm, Contentment, Excited, Frustrated, Glad, Happy, Sad, Tired) evoked by artwork. 132,664 artworks across 56 artistic styles; preview dataset EmoArt-5k has 5,532 examples. Images distributed in category-specific .tar.gz archives on HuggingFace - must be downloaded separately. Adapted from text-to-image generation benchmark to vision-language classification task. Evaluates models' understanding of emotional content in artistic creativity. See scenarios/emoart/evaluation_notes.md for detailed methodology.

name: Outline to Story (O2S)
notes: Controllable story generation from writing prompts; uses WritingPrompts dataset (euclaise/writingprompts); 15,138 test examples, 15,620 validation; prompts serve as outlines/guidance for multi-paragraph story generation; stories typically 500-2000 words; supports max_instances parameter to limit dataset size; open-ended generation evaluation

name: Real Satirical Photographs Dataset
notes: Multimodal (vision-language); PIL images saved to temp files; 1,075 valid examples with difficulty labels (EASY: 954, MEDIUM: 107, HARD: 14)

name: Persona Generation Task
notes: Original URL (vijetadeshpande/Diverse-NS) was 404; correct repo: text-machine-lab/diverse-not-short. Paper: 'Diverse, not Short' (EMNLP 2025, arXiv:2505.16245). Six creativity tasks: RAT (144 items, exact_match), AUT (15 objects), CWT (7 word-triplets), DAT (1 prompt), C-DAT (15 words), PGT (1 prompt). RAT has labeled answers; others are open-ended. Multi-seed diversity evaluation (100 seeds for DAT/PGT, 10 for CWT/AUT). HF dataset: text-machine-lab/diverse-not-short (6K preference pairs for DPO training). Note: DAT/C-DAT tasks overlap with existing dat_creative_writing and cdat scenarios but use different prompts/test sets from this paper's framework.

name: MeLBench
reason: Multimodal (image + text → audio); requires audio evaluation framework. CVPR 2024, arXiv:2406.04673; 'MeLFusion: Synthesizing Music from Image and Language Cues using Diffusion Models'; MeLBench is dataset introduced to facilitate music synthesis research supporting MeLFusion multimodal music generation system; task: synthesize music from both image and language cues; input format: image + text description; output: generated music/audio files; example: given image of sunset and text 'calm evening music', generate appropriate music; uses diffusion model with novel 'visual synapse' that infuses visual semantics into music generation; built on AudioLDM and Tango architectures; evaluation metrics: IMSM (Image-Music Similarity Metric, newly proposed), FAD (Fréchet Audio Distance for audio quality), plus objective and subjective assessments; performance: adding visual information improves music quality by up to 67.98% on FAD score; compared against MusicLM, Moûsai, MusicGen; requires processing images and text to generate audio; requires audio generation diffusion models and audio quality evaluation; outside HELM's text-only scope; would need audio generation evaluation framework; GitHub: schowdhury671/melfusion; project page: schowdhury671.github.io/melfusion_cvpr2024; dataset available via OneDrive link

name: Learn2Gen
reason: Method paper presenting training framework (SFT + RL) for research idea generation model, not an evaluation benchmark; collected 6,765 ICLR/NeurIPS papers (2023-2024) for training their LDC model but provides no public test set with ground truth for benchmarking arbitrary LLMs; evaluation focuses exclusively on validating their model using GPT-4 reviewer with retrieval-augmented scoring; GitHub repository currently empty with no code/data release; arXiv:2412.14626
paper: LDC: Learning to Generate Research Idea with Dynamic Control (December 2024)
notes: Similar to The AI Scientist, CodeScientist, and Scientist-Bench - research automation system rather than evaluation benchmark. Evaluates ideas on novelty, feasibility, and effectiveness dimensions but through custom infrastructure.

name: SHOE SALES
reason: Domain-specific scientific reasoning; synthetic task in HypoBench for hypothesis generation from tabular data (predict shoe color from customer appearance); requires structured data input and inference testing; not general text creativity; HDR metric compares against ground-truth hypotheses

name: Realistic-Fantasy Benchmark (RFBench)
reason: Creativity benchmark for text-to-image diffusion models (ECCV 2024). 229 prompts with a strong creativity taxonomy (metaphorical thinking, counterfactual scenarios, anthropomorphism, role reversal). However, the creative output being evaluated is generated images, not text. Dataset contains only prompts + category labels — no ground-truth outputs, annotations, or rubrics to evaluate LLM/VLM responses against. Prompts could theoretically be repurposed for text tasks, but that would require building a new benchmark, not onboarding this one.

name: Chinese Essay Rhetoric Dataset (CERD)
notes: Dataset not publicly available. Comprehensive Chinese rhetoric dataset with 503 essays covering 4 coarse-grained categories (metaphor, personification, hyperbole, parallelism) and 23 fine-grained categories. Five sub-tasks: rhetoric classification, form classification, content classification, component extraction, and rhetorical sentence generation. GitHub README states 'please contact via email at nwliu@stu.ecnu.edu.cn' for access. Not available on HuggingFace or for direct download. Paper: EMNLP 2024 Findings (arXiv:2409.19691). May be released publicly in future.

name: Research Outcome Prediction Benchmark
reason: Research study, not evaluation benchmark; comparative execution study of 43 researchers implementing LLM vs human ideas (100+ hours each); pre-computed results showing LLM ideas' scores decreased more post-execution (ideation-execution gap); one-time comparison not reusable for evaluating arbitrary models; similar to Future Research Idea Generation study; Stanford/ICLR 2025; arXiv:2506.20803

name: Research Ideation Evaluation Framework
reason: Method/system paper, not benchmark; Budget AI Researcher RAG-based idea generator; comparative evaluation vs baselines (GPT-4o-mini, Claude 3.5); human evaluation primary (interestingness, novelty, feasibility); no standardized test set for new models; repository contains system code

name: Verbal Fluency Task
notes: Paper: 'Characterising the Creative Process in Humans and LLMs' (ICCC 2024, arXiv:2405.00899). Three tasks: VF (30 animals), AUT brick (30 uses), AUT paperclip (20 uses). Each is a single prompt repeated N times (default 5, matching paper's 5 reps). Process analysis via gte-large embeddings: semantic similarity chains, category clustering, jump profiles. Human baseline: 219 Dutch participants. 8 LLM baselines at multiple temperatures.

name: MSCOCO with Abstract Visual Associations and Creative Captions
reason: Valuable creativity resource but not an onboardable benchmark (Columbia University, July 2025). However, it's a training data pipeline — no dedicated test instances to evaluate models against. Downstream creativity evaluation happens on existing external benchmarks (MultiM-Poem, HAIVMet/VisualMetaphors) which could potentially be onboarded separately. Data on GitHub + Google Drive.

name: Puntuguese

However, requires embodied execution in a running Minecraft instance — no text-representable output format (unlike JSON coordinates in layout tasks). Only 20 test instructions. 29.4 GB training data on Zenodo. Related but separate from MineAnyBuild (NeurIPS 2025).

name: RICO
reason: Dataset and code not publicly available. Paper: 'Aggregated Structural Representation with Large Language Models for Human-Centric Layout Generation' (arXiv:2505.19554, May 26, 2025). Uses filtered RICO dataset with 68,475 UI structures but filtering process and preprocessing code not released. Original RICO dataset exists (HuggingFace: Voxel51/rico, shunk031/Rico) but paper's filtered version with specific preprocessing is unavailable. No GitHub repository found (authors from Ant Group, A*STAR). Task: UI layout generation from graph structures with nodes (UI components: background, image, text, input, sliding bar, icon) and edges (positional relations: TOP, LEFT; semantic relations: PARALLEL, CONTAIN). Output format: JSON with node_id, category, coordinates [X,Y,W,H], and relation arrays. Three subtasks: (1) UI-Gen: direct generation from scratch, (2) Completion: generate with node/edge constraints, (3) Graph Editing: human-in-the-loop editing. Evaluation metrics: mIoU, Relation Error (RE), FID, Overlap (OL), human study (50 participants, 0-5 Likert scale on reasonableness). Model: ASR combines GNN (graph representation) + Intern-VL (MLLM) with relation matrix decoder. Multimodal benchmark (processes icon images, component images, text) - can be onboarded with HEIM once dataset/code released. Contact: jin_jiongchao@ihpc.a-star.edu.sg. Monitor for release.

Not a standardized benchmark for text generation. NeurIPS 2024. Dataset on HuggingFace. arXiv:2407.09388.

name: KiVA (Kid-inspired Visual Analogies)
reason: Multimodal (vision-language); requires HEIM/VHELM framework. ICLR 2025, arXiv:2407.17773; visual analogical reasoning benchmark with 4,300 visual transformations of everyday objects; tests fundamental visual pattern recognition skills solvable by children ages 3-5; 5 transformation domains (2D Rotation, Color, Resize, Reflection, Counting) with 14-29 subdomains; two difficulty levels: KiVA (easy, solvable by 3-year-olds) and KiVA-adults (hard, different input values requiring further abstraction); task format: given images showing object transformation (e.g., blue dog → red dog), identify which option (A/B/C) applies the same transformation to a new object; three evaluation stages: identify what changed, how it changed, apply rule to new scenarios; evaluates large multimodal models (GPT-4V, GPT-o1, LLaVA-1.5, MANTIS) compared to human children and adults; findings show models identify 'what' changed but struggle with quantifying 'how' and extrapolating rules; repository contains 96K+ files including transformed object images in both stitched format (single image) and individual format (multiple images); requires vision-language models and visual processing; outside HELM's text-only scope; would need HEIM/VHELM framework; GitHub: ey242/KiVA
notes: ICLR 2025 visual analogical reasoning benchmark. 2,100 total instances (700 unique trials × 3 repetitions). Each trial repeated 3 times with randomized answer positions. Multimodal (vision-language) 3-way MC task testing fundamental pattern recognition skills solvable by 3-5 year old children. Scenario supports deduplicate=True to use only unique trials (700 instances) and avoid position bias. Evaluation: exact_match accuracy. Human baseline (children ages 3-5): ~80-90%. Best LMM (GPT-o1): ~60-70%. Data auto-downloaded from GitHub release (single_image.zip, 77MB). Standard prompt: 'Which one of three transformations is the same as the top transformation?' Test split only.

name: Mathematical Framework for Objective Characterization of Ideas
reason: Method paper, not benchmark; Proposes mathematical framework for evaluating idea quality/diversity in product design using embeddings (UMAP, DBSCAN, PCA); validates on 6 problem statements with 100 CAI-generated ideas each (600 total) but data not publicly released; software 'not yet been publicly released'; tool for product designers to select promising ideas, not for benchmarking LLMs; no standardized test set with ground truth; arXiv:2409.07578; September 2024 (updated May 2025)

name: CLEF JOKER 2025 Task 2: Wordplay Translation
notes: English→French pun translation preserving wordplay. Dataset gated behind CLEF 2025 registration (Codabench) — not on HuggingFace. Load from local JSON (output_path/joker_2025_task2_train.json). Train split used as TEST_SPLIT (1,405 puns / 5,838 French translations); test French translations not publicly released. JSON fields: id_en, en, fr — multiple objects per pun grouped by en. Prompt avoids 'translate'; asks for French pun reconstruction. Official metric: BLEU; BERTScore + human eval in metric_notes.md. arXiv:2507.06506; CEUR-WS Vol-4038 paper_219.

name: P4I (PoemForImage) Dataset
notes: 3,008 poems with summaries and per-segment emotion annotations. Adapted as text-only: summary+emotions -> poem generation (original image outputs not published). Data in Segmented_Poems.csv via git clone. max_instances parameter for subsampling.

name: Diversity vs. Recognizability Framework
reason: Multimodal (image generation); requires HEIM framework. ICML 2023, arXiv:2301.11722; 'Diffusion Models as Artists: Are we Closing the Gap between Humans and Machines?'; evaluation framework for one-shot generative models comparing humans and machines on one-shot image generation task; extends 'diversity vs. recognizability' framework (Boutin et al., 2022, arXiv:2205.10370) to evaluate diffusion models (DDPM, CFGDM, FSDM) alongside GANs and VAEs; three evaluation metrics: (1) Recognizability - how recognizable generated images are, (2) Diversity - intra-class variability in generated samples, (3) Originality - measured via generalization curves showing evolution of recognizability as function of originality; evaluated on Omniglot dataset (handwritten characters, 1,320 models tested) and QuickDraw dataset (hand-drawn sketches, 1,212 models tested); task: given one example of handwritten character or sketch, generate diverse yet recognizable variations; findings show diffusion models have closed gap between humans and machines but humans still produce more recognizable samples at higher originality levels; human features are fewer and more localized than diffusion model features; requires training diffusion models on image datasets and evaluating generated images; datasets available via Google Drive; outside HELM's text-only scope; would need HEIM framework; GitHub: serre-lab/diffusion_as_artist

name: Sudoku-Bench
notes: Three subsets: challenge_100, nikoli_100, ctc. Evaluation: exact_match on 81-digit solution

name: GraphicBench
reason: Original adobe-research repo still 404. Repo exists at github.com/dayeonki/graphicbench (personal account) but has no LICENSE file. Work done during Adobe Research internship; never published under Adobe's org, likely missing open-source approval. No license = all rights reserved by default.

name: Outline-Conditioned Story Generation
reason: Method paper, not a reusable benchmark. PlotMachines (EMNLP 2020) is a model architecture paper; no publicly available preprocessed test data with outlines; requires downloading WikiPlots/WritingPrompts/NYT and running complex preprocessing pipeline (RAKE outline extraction); no standardized evaluation protocol that other papers follow. Better-defined benchmarks exist for this task (e.g., 'Outline to Story (O2S)' assigned to VD with actual benchmark dataset).

name: Poetry Generation Evaluation
reason: Duplicate entry — same anonymous URL as 'Thinking Outside the (Gray) Box' (line ~3586, already marked not_suitable). Methods paper by Franceschelli & Musolesi proposing CoVO (Context-based Value and Originality) score as RL reward signal. Introduces GutenVerse (~84k poems) as reference corpus for originality metric, not an evaluation benchmark. No standardized test set or evaluation protocol. Evaluates on existing benchmarks (NoveltyBench, GSM8K, MATH). Anonymous link also inaccessible.

name: Codeforces
notes: Mislabeled entry — actual benchmark is AidanBench (NeurIPS 2024 Workshop), not Codeforces; no competitive programming content. 66 open-ended creativity questions hardcoded from GitHub. Original protocol is multi-turn (sequential generation until coherence ≤15/100 or novelty ≤0.15); adapted to single-turn batch prompting (N=30 responses). Empty references; custom metrics required: Self-BLEU (diversity), LLM coherence judge (o1-mini), embedding novelty — see metric_notes.md. OpenReview: fz969ahcvJ.

name: Standard Science Analogies (STD)
notes: SAQA dataset: 109 unique science concepts, 148 reference analogies from Q&A sites. nosrc: generate analogy without source (109 instances). wsrc: generate analogy with given source concept (148 instances). Data downloaded from GitHub repo at runtime.

name: Human Evaluation of Suspenseful Story Generation
reason: Methodology paper with human evaluation, not a benchmark dataset. EACL 2024, arXiv:2402.17119; paper titled 'Creating Suspenseful Stories: Iterative Planning with Large Language Models' by Kaige Xie and Mark Riedl; proposes novel iterative-prompting-based planning method grounded in cognitive psychology and narratology theories of suspense; zero-shot approach using ChatGPT (gpt-3.5-turbo-0613) and Llama 2 (Llama-2-13b-chat); conducted human evaluation study on Prolific with 90 participants evaluating 30 story pairs (10 pairs each) on 5 criteria: Suspense, Novelty, Enjoyment, Logical Sense, Naturalness; compared proposed method against baselines (vanilla ChatGPT/Llama2, Re3) and ablations; no public dataset or code repository found (author GitHub: lightyear0117 has no related repos); no test prompts, story examples, or evaluation protocols released; evaluation was one-time human study to validate their specific method, not a reusable benchmark for comparing arbitrary LLMs; paper provides detailed prompts in tables but these are method-specific; similar to In-the-Wild Study - evaluates a proposed method rather than providing standardized benchmark for LLM comparison

name: Divergent Association Task (DAT)
notes: Models generate 10 unrelated nouns; creativity scored by average cosine distance between word pairs using GloVe 840B embeddings. 100 independent trials by default (same prompt repeated). No ground truth references — evaluated entirely by custom DATMetric. Human baseline mean DAT ~78, SD ~10 (8,572 responses). Requires custom metric implementation; see metric_notes.md.

name: FIGR-8-SVG
notes: Vector graphics generation benchmark, outside HELM scope. Text-to-SVG icon synthesis (IconShop, Siggraph Asia 2023). 1.5M monochromatic vector icons across 17,375 classes (pictograms, ideograms, emoticons). Input: text keywords/descriptions. Output: SVG vector graphics (geometric paths, commands). Evaluates semantic alignment, novelty, diversity, structural integrity. For visual autoregressive models (IconShop vs VectorFusion, SVGDreamer, Chat2SVG), not text-based LLMs. Requires image generation evaluation framework. arXiv:2304.14400.

name: TRIG-Bench
reason: Text-to-image generation benchmark; evaluates image generation with text rendering, not VLM creativity

name: Imitative Editing Benchmark
reason: Image-to-image task (outputs edited images, not text); dataset not yet released (verified Feb 2026). NeurIPS 2024, arXiv:2406.07547; MimicBrush method for zero-shot image editing with reference imitation; introduces 'imitative editing' task where users draw inspiration from in-the-wild references to edit image regions; benchmark has 120 samples collected from Pexels across 4 topics (fashion, animals, products, scenarios) with 30 samples per topic; two main tasks: (1) Part Composition - discovering semantic correspondence between source and reference images and compositing local parts, (2) Texture Transfer - transferring texture from reference to source image; each task has inter-ID and inner-ID tracks; task format: INPUT (source image + reference image + mask) → OUTPUT (edited image that imitates reference); evaluation metrics: fidelity (DINO/CLIP similarity), harmonization (blending quality), visual quality; GitHub README still states 'Download our evaluation benchmark at Google Drive: URL: [to be released]' as of Feb 2026 (repo last pushed June 2024); Note: Image INPUT is supported by HELM (see EmoArt scenario using MediaObject), but this task requires IMAGE GENERATION output, not text output; original evaluation requires comparing generated edited images to references using visual similarity metrics; could potentially be adapted to text-based task (e.g., edit description generation, edit quality classification) if dataset becomes available; GitHub: ali-vilab/MimicBrush

name: STYLEBREEDER
reason: Image generation benchmark, not LLM benchmark; Evaluates text-to-image diffusion models (Stable Diffusion, SD-XL, ControlNet), not language models; 6.8M images + 1.8M prompts from 95K Artbreeder users; three tasks: style discovery (K-Means clustering), personalized image generation (LoRA, Textual Inversion, Custom Diffusion), style recommendation (matrix factorization); metrics: CLIP-I, CLIP-T, DINO for image quality; outside HELM scope (requires HEIM framework for image generation); gated dataset (requires HuggingFace authentication); CC0 license; NeurIPS 2024; stylebreeder.github.io; arXiv:2406.14599

name: ArtInsight Artwork Description Evaluation
notes: 30 children's artwork JPEG images in Artwork-Description-Scoring/images/. Task: generate description for BLV parents. Open-ended generation, no gold text reference. Prompt reconstructed from README optimal system prompt description. Images downloaded via urllib from GitHub raw URLs (URL-encode spaces in filenames). name: Prompt Embedding Manipulation Evaluation / Aesthetic Quality Benchmark
notes: Text-to-image aesthetic quality evaluation using curated prompts from DiffusionDB and LAION-Aesthetics-V2. While the original paper focused on embedding manipulation techniques, we adapted it into a HEIM benchmark by using their curated prompts (149 DiffusionDB + 13 LAION = 162 total) as a test set for evaluating aesthetic quality in text-to-image generation. Prompts are highly detailed, creative, and span diverse artistic styles (fantasy art, concept design, landscapes, character illustration, photorealistic scenes). Evaluation metrics: LAION Aesthetic Predictor V2 (primary), image quality (sharpness/blurriness), CLIP score (alignment). Tests models' ability to generate aesthetically pleasing, high-quality creative outputs. Model-agnostic - works with any text-to-image model (Stable Diffusion, DALL-E, Midjourney, etc.). See scenarios/prompt_embedding_manipulation/evaluation_notes.md for detailed methodology.

name: S-DAT (Synthetic-Divergent Association Task)

name: Material Generation Benchmark (MP-20)

test.description: Text-to-structure: Generate CIF format crystal structures from material specifications

notes: Text-to-structure generation task. MP-20 dataset: 45,231 stable materials from Materials Project/ICSD with 1-20 atoms per unit cell, 89 elements. LLMs generate crystal structures in CIF format given composition and properties (formula, space group, formation energy, band gap, energy above hull). Evaluation: Custom structural matching metrics required (match rate, RMSD, validity, chemical correctness, physical plausibility) - see metric_notes.md. Requires pymatgen/ASE for structure comparison. Data source: CDVAE repo (https://github.com/txie-93/cdvae). Paper: MGB: The Material Generation Benchmark (OpenReview 2025).

name: Material Generation Benchmark (PEROV-5)
notes: Text-to-structure generation for perovskites. PEROV-5 dataset: 18,928 perovskite materials (ABX3 formula) from water-splitting database, all with 5 atoms per unit cell, 56 elements. LLMs generate CIF structures given formula and properties (heat of formation, band gaps). Evaluation: Same custom metrics as MP-20. Data source: CDVAE repo. Paper: MGB (OpenReview 2025).

name: Material Generation Benchmark (Carbon-24)
notes: Text-to-structure generation for carbon allotropes. Carbon-24 dataset: 10,153 carbon structures with 6-24 atoms per unit cell from AIRSS at 10 GPa. LLMs generate CIF structures given energy per atom. Evaluation: Same custom metrics as MP-20. Data source: CDVAE repo. Paper: MGB (OpenReview 2025).

name: Material Generation Benchmark (MOF)

test.description: MOF (Metal-Organic Framework) structure generation from building blocks

notes: Text-to-structure generation for Metal-Organic Frameworks. MOFFlow dataset: 324,426 MOF structures from Boyd et al. (2019), filtered for ≥200 blocks, split 8:1:1 train/valid/test. LLMs generate CIF structures given metal nodes, organic linkers, and topology. More complex than simple crystals (hundreds of atoms, rigid building blocks). Baseline: MOFFlow achieves 31.69% match rate on unseen structures. Evaluation: Structural matching, validity, physical plausibility. Data source: Zenodo (15187230). Paper: MOFFlow (ICLR 2025). Used in MGB paper for MOF structure prediction task.

name: Materials Transformers (ICSD-mix)
notes: Chemical formula generation in expanded element form. ICSD-mix: 52,317 materials from Inorganic Crystal Structure Database with mixed purity (includes charge-imbalanced samples). Task: Open-ended generation of compositions like 'Li Li O .' (Li₂O). Evaluation: Validity (charge neutrality 97.54%, electronegativity balance 91.40%), uniqueness, recovery rate, novelty (6x better than random). Dataset: Figshare MT_dataset. Paper: Fu et al. 2022 Materials Transformers.

name: Materials Transformers (ICSD-pure)
notes: Chemical formula generation (filtered for charge neutrality). ICSD-pure: 39,431 charge-neutral materials from ICSD. Task: Generate valid formulas in expanded element form. Evaluation: Same metrics as ICSD-mix (validity, uniqueness, novelty). Cleaner dataset for testing model performance on well-formed compositions. Dataset: Figshare MT_dataset.

name: Materials Transformers (Hybrid-mix)
notes: Chemical formula generation (largest dataset). Hybrid-mix: 418,983 materials from ICSD+Materials Project+OQMD, mixed purity. Most diverse benchmark combining multiple materials databases. Task: Generate novel material compositions. Evaluation: Validity, uniqueness, recovery rate, novelty. Tests generalization across different data sources. Dataset: Figshare MT_dataset.

name: Materials Transformers (Hybrid-pure)
notes: Chemical formula generation (charge-neutral hybrid). Hybrid-pure: 257,138 materials from ICSD+MP+OQMD filtered for charge neutrality. Large, clean dataset for testing compositional generation. Evaluation: Validity, uniqueness, novelty. Dataset: Figshare MT_dataset.

name: Materials Transformers (Hybrid-strict)
notes: Chemical formula generation (strictest filtering). Hybrid-strict: 212,778 materials from ICSD+MP+OQMD with strict quality filters (charge neutrality + electronegativity balance). Highest quality subset for testing model on well-validated compositions. Evaluation: Validity, uniqueness, novelty. Dataset: Figshare MT_dataset.

name: Materials Transformers (Bandgap-30K)
notes: Property-conditional formula generation (wide-bandgap materials). Bandgap-30K: ~30K materials from Materials Project with bandgap > 1.98 eV. Task: Generate high-bandgap material compositions. Tests property-targeted generation and bandgap prediction capability. Evaluation: Validity, uniqueness, novelty, plus optional bandgap validation. Dataset: Figshare MT_dataset (mp/ folder).

name: Amuse - Chord Progression Generation

test.description: Diversity evaluation: Generate 30 diverse 4-bar chord progressions per music keyword

notes: Music chord progression generation from keywords. Task: Generate diverse chord progressions given music keywords (e.g., 'Groovy', 'Melancholy'), musical key, and mode. 254 music keywords from suno.wiki. Evaluation: Custom diversity metrics (Self-BLEU - lower = more diverse) and coherence metrics (Jensen-Shannon Divergence against Hooktheory dataset). Paper evaluates batch prompting (30 progressions at once) vs. conventional prompting (iterative). Amuse achieves Self-BLEU 0.30±0.12 vs. baseline 0.61±0.18. No ground truth references - generative task evaluated by distributional metrics. Requires Hooktheory dataset (26,175 songs) for JSD calculation. CHI 2025 paper. See metric_notes.md for Self-BLEU and JSD implementation.

name: FunQA
reason: Video-based benchmark; outside HELM scope
notes: Video question-answering benchmark requiring actual video files. 4.3K video clips (24 hours) with 312K free-text QA pairs across HumorQA (1,769 clips), CreativeQA (927 clips), and MagicQA (1,672 clips). Tasks: timestamp localization, video description, reasoning, title generation, creativity scoring (1-20 scale). Paper states '86% thought FunQA cannot be solved only by images.' HELM doesn't support video understanding tasks—requires video processing infrastructure. Dataset: fesvhtr/FunQA on HuggingFace, GitHub: Jingkang50/FunQA. License: CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0. ECCV 2024. CreativeQA has creativity components but benchmark fundamentally requires video modality.

name: Sonnet or Not, Bot?

all.description: Poetry form recognition across all form groups

verse forms.description: Recognize verse forms: sonnet, ballad, haiku, limerick, sestina, villanelle, ghazal, pantoum

types/modes.description: Recognize poetic types/modes: elegy, ode, pastoral, dramatic monologue, ekphrasis, etc.

meters.description: Recognize metrical forms: common measure, blank verse, free verse

notes: Poetry form recognition task. Models classify poems into poetic forms (sonnet, haiku, ballad, etc.) across 4 form groups: verse forms (8 types), stanza forms (2 types), types/modes (9 types), meters (3 types). 1,453 public domain poems with expert annotations. EMNLP Findings 2024. Evaluation: F1, precision, recall. Human baseline: 67% accuracy on sonnets, 53% on ballads. GitHub: https://github.com/maria-antoniak/poetry-eval

name: POLLUX - Russian Creativity

literary_text.description: Write literary texts (stories, poems, narratives) in Russian

creative_brainstorming.description: Generate creative ideas and brainstorm solutions

style_transfer.description: Adapt text across different styles and registers

all_creative.description: All creativity tasks combined (deduplicated unique instructions)

notes: Russian-language creativity evaluation benchmark. 35 task types total, scenario filters for 6-7 creativity-related types: literary text (6,764), creative brainstorming (5,558), text interpretation (6,081), style transfer (5,977), AI as character (6,025), applied brainstorming (6,452). Total ~36K creative examples from 161K total dataset. Evaluation: LLM-as-a-Judge with detailed criteria (0-4 scale) including Creativity, Dramaturgy, Dialogue Expressiveness, Genre Appropriateness, Rhyme Quality, Verse Meter, Literary Accents, Character Adherence. Dataset has multiple model outputs per instruction (7 models), scenario deduplicates to ~2,115 unique instructions per task type (~10K total creative). Expert annotations included (24,447 hours, $262K cost). Key finding: SOTA models (Claude 3.5 Sonnet, o1) lag humans on creativity, criticized for 'lack of soul'. Judge models available: ai-forever/pollux-judge-7b-r and pollux-judge-32b-r. HuggingFace: ai-forever/POLLUX. See annotator_notes.md for detailed criteria. December 2025 paper.

name: CDAT

all.description: Generate 10 mutually dissimilar nouns related to cue word

notes: Conditional Divergent Association Task - evaluates divergent creative thinking through word generation. Task: Generate 10 dissimilar nouns that are each associated with a given cue word. Tests both novelty (how different words are from each other) and appropriateness (how related to cue). Evaluation: Custom metrics using word embeddings (FastText/GloVe) - Appropriateness (similarity to cue), Novelty (pairwise distance), Creativity Score (combined) - see metric_notes.md. 1,000 cue words from Brown corpus downloaded from GitHub. Addresses DAT limitation which only measures novelty. EACL 2026 (Findings). Nakajima et al.

name: LeMat-GenBench (MOF/Crystal Generation)
reason: Materials science evaluation, not creativity
notes: Standardized evaluation framework for crystal generative models. Evaluates thermodynamic viability and scientific validity (stability, novelty, validity) NOT creative quality. Requires specialized materials science software (pymatgen, MLIP ensembles, MACE-MP, UMA, Orb-v3) for crystallographic analysis and energy predictions. Models generate CIF (Crystallographic Information File) format. Metrics: energy above convex hull, charge neutrality, structural fingerprinting. Evaluates 12 generative models on unconditional generation of 2,500 structures. GitHub: LeMaterial/lemat-genbench. Public leaderboard on HuggingFace Spaces. Focuses on scientific correctness not creativity. December 2024.

name: L2M3OF (MOF Structure-Property)
reason: Model paper, not creativity benchmark
notes: Multimodal LLM for Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs). Introduces MOF-SPK dataset (133,737 MOF structures from CCDC, 35,000+ publications). Four tasks: property prediction, structure extraction (SMILES), description generation, Q&A. Evaluates scientific understanding and property prediction NOT creative generation. Temporal split (pre-2020 train, post-2022 test). Evaluation: MAE for properties, BLEU/EXACT for structures, GPT-4-mini for head-to-head comparisons. Borderline creativity—focuses on knowledge extraction and prediction rather than creative synthesis. Requires molecular encoders for multimodal components. October 2024.

name: Thinking Outside the (Gray) Box
reason: Methods paper, not a benchmark. Paper by Franceschelli & Musolesi proposes CoVO (Context-based Value and Originality) score as a reward signal for RL fine-tuning. Introduces GutenVerse (~84k poems from Project Gutenberg) as a reference corpus for measuring originality via T-LCS, not as an evaluation benchmark with test prompts. Paper evaluates their training method on existing benchmarks: NoveltyBench (Zhang et al. 2025), GSM8K, and MATH. GutenVerse is similar to using a large corpus for perplexity - it's a resource for computing metrics, not a benchmark itself. No standardized test set or evaluation protocol released. Note: NoveltyBench (separate benchmark) could be onboarded separately.
notes: GutenVerse corpus buildable from https://anonymous.4open.science/r/GutenVerse-DD32/

name: SS-GEN
notes: Social Story generation for children with autism. Constrained creative writing (200-300 words) with 8 therapeutic criteria. Evaluation: BLEU/ROUGE metrics + human evaluation (Structural Clarity, Descriptive Orientation, Situational Safety) + GPT-4 judge (Coherence, Descriptiveness, Empathy, Grammaticality, Relevance). Dataset on GitHub in JSONL format. AAAI 2025 Oral presentation.

name: DataNarrative
notes: Data-driven storytelling benchmark. Task: Generate narrative paragraphs from tabular data, describing trends, patterns, and insights. Multi-agent framework with iterative refinement: Reflection (analyze data) → Outline (structure story) → Narration (write story), each with critique and revision stages. Prompts from Figures 18-26 in appendix. Evaluation: BLEU/ROUGE + GPT-4 judge (factual accuracy, coherence, comprehensiveness, theme consistency) + human evaluation. Sources: Tableau (226 train, 59 test), Pew Research (1,590 test), GapMinder (42 test). Each story has multiple paragraph-table segments. Scenario creates one instance per segment. EMNLP 2024. See annotator_notes.md for multi-stage framework details.
